quiz.title: Adding and Subtracting Fractions Quiz
quiz.instructions: Choose one answer for each question. Give answers as fractions in their simplest form; an improper fraction is allowed.

questions.prompt: Calculate \(\frac{2}{9}+\frac{4}{9}\). Give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form.
Calculate \(\frac{7}{10}-\frac{3}{10}\). Give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form.
Calculate \(\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{2}\). Give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form.
questions.working:
Use a common denominator of 4.

\(\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{2}=\frac{1}{4}+\frac{2}{4}=\frac{3}{4}\).

\(\frac{3}{4}\) is already in its simplest form.

questions.prompt: Calculate \(\frac{5}{6}-\frac{1}{3}\). Give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form.
Calculate \(\frac{2}{3}+\frac{1}{4}\). Give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form.
questions.working:
Use a common denominator of 12.

\(\frac{2}{3}+\frac{1}{4}=\frac{8}{12}+\frac{3}{12}=\frac{11}{12}\).

\(\frac{11}{12}\) is already in its simplest form.

questions.prompt: Calculate \(\frac{7}{8}-\frac{1}{4}\). Give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form.
questions.working:
Use a common denominator of 8.

\(\frac{7}{8}-\frac{1}{4}=\frac{7}{8}-\frac{2}{8}=\frac{5}{8}\).

\(\frac{5}{8}\) is already in its simplest form.

questions.prompt: Calculate \(\frac{3}{5}+\frac{1}{6}\). Give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form.
questions.working:
Use a common denominator of 30.

\(\frac{3}{5}+\frac{1}{6}=\frac{18}{30}+\frac{5}{30}=\frac{23}{30}\).

\(\frac{23}{30}\) is already in its simplest form.

questions.prompt: Calculate \(\frac{5}{6}-\frac{3}{8}\). Give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form.
questions.working:
Use a common denominator of 24.

\(\frac{5}{6}-\frac{3}{8}=\frac{20}{24}-\frac{9}{24}=\frac{11}{24}\).

\(\frac{11}{24}\) is already in its simplest form.

questions.prompt: Calculate \(\frac{3}{4}+\frac{2}{3}\). Give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form.
questions.working:
Use a common denominator of 12.

\(\frac{3}{4}+\frac{2}{3}=\frac{9}{12}+\frac{8}{12}=\frac{17}{12}\).

\(\frac{17}{12}\) is already in its simplest form.

This is an improper fraction; it is also \(1\frac{5}{12}\).

questions.prompt: Calculate \(\frac{11}{12}-\frac{2}{5}\). Give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form.
questions.working:
Use a common denominator of 60.

\(\frac{11}{12}-\frac{2}{5}=\frac{55}{60}-\frac{24}{60}=\frac{31}{60}\).

\(\frac{31}{60}\) is already in its simplest form.
